headline: US Domestic Airfares Jump up to 25% as Jet Fuel Spike Drives Lasting Price Pressures
summary: Average domestic airfares rose across all 50 major US metro areas between April and June, climbing by up to 25% in cities like Detroit, as airlines passed on elevated fuel costs driven by geopolitical conflict.
why: Jet fuel represents one of the largest single operating costs for commercial passenger airlines, directly impacting passenger yields and consumer travel demand.

impacts.name: Airlines
impacts.why: Higher ticket prices help offset surging fuel input costs but risk curbing leisure travel demand if prices remain elevated.
